filesChanged: packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/store/store_test.go: the forward merge's one conflict, resolved to keep main's handoffs table and its three events_outbox_* indexes beside this change's document_search and search_term_queue, with asks_open_artifact gone.
packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/benchtime/subjects.go: Subjects carries ProbeLexemes, the project's twenty commonest words, read from search_term_stats as every other subject is.
packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/statement_timing_test.go: the relatedProbeSQL pair is measured on those twenty words rather than on the three the other statements use.
trickyParts: A plan-pair bound decides nothing on a subject where both plans do the same trivial work. At three lexemes the probe's document arm looks a handful of candidate documents up and the two texts are within a percent of each other either way, so the committed pair was red on three of four runs and green on one. The subject has to be where the statement does the work the change is about.

Both measurement databases must be measured at the same point in their own history. Taking the before side before the A9 rounds and the after side after them makes every protocol 2 'after' reading look worse than it is: listIssueAsksQueryAll read 324us that way and 1.101ms this way, on the same code.
deviations: The few-lexeme 'lower after' the previous round committed is withdrawn rather than fixed, on the architect's word: the reading is parity and is recorded in the pull request body as parity, with the four runs that show it and the reason.
discoveredComplexity: Main's own probe text costs 2.306873 s on main's schema and 20.775 ms on this release's, at the same twenty words on copies of one seed. The gap is asks_issue_key and messages_issue_roots, which this change adds and which the probe's ask and message arms use: most of the probe's gain is not in its own text at all.
